newsitem.title: USA: Foundation Health, Health Systems in merger.
newsitem.headline: Foundation Health, Health Systems in merger.

text.p: Foundation Health Corp. and Health Systems International Inc. said Tuesday they agreed to merge in a deal valued at about $3 billion, based on the companies' combined market capitalisation.
The combined company, called Foundation Health Systems, Inc., will be the nation's fourth-largest publicly traded managed care company, with 5 million medical members in 16 states.

On a pro forma basis, Foundation Health Systems would have recorded total annual revenues of $6.4 billion in the year ended June 30, 1996, and estimated revenues of more than $8 billion in calendar 1997.
Foundation and Health Systems said they expected annual savings of at least $110 million from the merger, which will be accounted for as a tax-free pooling of interests.

Under the definitive agreement approved by both companies' boards, each Foundation share will be exchanged for 1.3 Class A common shares of the new company. Each Health Systems Class A common share will become a share of Foundation Health Systems Class A common stock.
Rancho Cordova, Calif.-based Foundation's stockholders will own 61 percent of the new company's roughly 124 million shares, with Health Systems stockholders holding 39 percent.
The California Wellness Foundation, which owns 19.3 million Health Systems Class B non-voting shares, will retain a similar stake in the new company.

"The transaction will immediately establish Foundation Health as a major national player, with strong market positions in California and the West and rapidly growing operations in Texas, Florida and the Northeast," said Malik M. Hasan, chairman and chief executive officer of Health Systems.

"The combined product line will cover virtually every facet of managed health care, including conventional health maintenance organisations, Medicare-risk HMOs and other substantial government programmes, workers' compensation and speciality products."

The companies said they expect savings from consolidation of overhead and administration, merging overlapping operations such as California HMOs, cross-selling Foundation speciality products to Health Systems members, and benefits of combined medical contracting.

The deal is expected to close by the end of January 1997, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. The companies have agreed to pay each other a termination fee if the deal fails to close under certain circumstances.

Health Systems is one of the nation's largest managed health care organisations, with more than 1.9 million members in California, Colorado, Connecticut, Idaho, New Jersey, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Oregon and Washington. The company, with corporate offices in Woodland Hills, Calif., and Pueblo, Colo., also owns Preferred Health Network, Inc. a preferred provider organisation.

Foundation provides group, individual, Medicare, Medicaid and Civilian Health and Medical Programme of the Uniformed Services coverage for more than three million individuals. The company's subsidiaries offer managed care products related to workers' compensation, behavioural health, dental, vision and prescription drugs, and administrative services for medical groups and self-funded benefits programmes.
Foundation's stock rose 25 cents to $34.125, while Health Systems gained 37.5 cents to $28.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
